data.body:
### [2/3] CORRECTED FALSE PREMISES — three errors caught by adversarial review, all previously believed true

E1. "A history rewrite creates UNRELATED histories, so sync.py:96's no-merge-base branch fires." FALSE. `.bridge_state` first appears 2026-06-11, so the first 1,029 commits are BYTE-IDENTICAL after a strip and `merge-base HEAD origin/tickets` SUCCEEDS (measured). Control reaches the ordinary DIVERGED path (sync.py:100-112) and unions normally. The hazard is real; the mechanism was mis-identified. Quiescence alone does NOT close it.

E2. "A guard in sync.py protects all writers." FALSE. push.py:203 and :229 run an INDEPENDENT `git merge <remote>/<branch>` on non-fast-forward rejection and then re-push (<=3 attempts), never consulting sync.py. That is exactly the path a stale review-bot write takes: voter.py:735 -> create_ticket -> push_after_commit -> push_tickets_branch -> rejected -> push.py:203 merge -> retry SUCCEEDS. A sync-only guard is bypassed and ~1 GiB returns silently.

E3. "Text-normalizing the baseline needs no migration because _extract_jira_field reads both shapes." FALSE-ish: `_extract_jira_field`/`_diff_fields` have ZERO production callers. The live path is outbound_field_diff.py:194 -> inbound_mapper.map_remote_to_local -> inbound_fields.py. Description/status/priority ARE safe there (canonicalized at READ time, idempotent on already-normalized values). ASSIGNEE IS NOT: _assignee_candidates (outbound_field_diff.py:56-67) unions the scalar with every non-None identity form; collapsing three forms to one string loses inbound-directionality suppression and local-wins silently CLOBBERS a concurrent remote assignee edit. Exclude assignee.

ALSO CORRECTED: (a) rebar NEVER clones - `grep 'git clone' src/` yields only a docstring - so it cannot filter a clone it does not perform; only the actions/checkout `filter:` input reduces a real transfer, and the tickets objects arrive in that 237s checkout step, NOT the 2s manual worktree mount. (b) `_ref_lock.py:347` is NOT a tickets fetch (it fetches refs/reconciler/{lock,gate}, read back via `cat-file blob`); filtering it would add promisor round-trips to the distributed lock. (c) `git blame` IS on a rebar path - metrics/blame.py:69 <- derive_caused_by <- transition_close.py:513, on every bug close without --caused-by - and PARTIAL blame failure is not benign: derive_caused_by tallies across paths and a subset can elect a culprit that would not have won, i.e. a WRONG caused_by link.
